text.p: Following are the main stories in Wednesday's Malaysian newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-- The government assumed a more pivotal role in the preparation and organisation of the 1998 Commonwealth Games by placing its entire machinery at the disposal of the organising committee.

-- The private sector should play a bigger role to help turn Malaysia into a centre of educational excellence as it is not possible for the government to fulfil all the needs of the society, Edcuation Minister Najib Razak said.

-- Aishah Jane Abdullah is back in Britain with her two-year-old son Sunni after fleeing to Bangkok over the weekend. Aishah, a British citizen, and her Malaysian husband have been embroiled in a custody battle over the child.

-- Second Board counter S & P Food Industries (M) Bhd is buying controlling stakes in another listed company and a financial services house as well as a substantial interest in stockbroking firm in its latest diversification drive.

-- As current regulatory boundaries no longer reflect the reality in the financial services industry, functional regulation of Malaysia's capital market will be the new focus of the authorities, Securities Commission chairman Munir Majid says.
-- In an unnannounced evacuation exercise, 121 Malaysians, including 11 infants, were airlifted out of Phnom Penh last night on board a Malaysia Airlines 737-400.
-- The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange is believed to be taking steps to bring the Kuala Lumpur Options and Financial Futures Exchange under its wings.
